newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds seen trading slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds seen trading slightly firmer.

text.p: Argentine bonds were seen slightly firmer as local traders do not expect U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to make big announcements in his Congressional testimony Tuesday.
"I see a firmer market with some more volume," a dealer for a huge local bank said. "We are pretty optimistic. Greenspan is not expected to shock the markets."
Another dealer for a local bank said the market could trade slightly firmer Tuesday, but will probably face a light correction in the next few days.
"The Argentine market is overbought and this rise may offer a good opportunity to sell," he said.
Dealers said the local market has also benefitted from a calmer situation in South East Asia and Brazil.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 edged up 1/4 percent to $94.375 against a previous close of 94.125, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was trading up 0.04 at 118.25.
